mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) indicates strengthening labor market conditions that boost consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 55% of months with PAYEMS growth exceeding 100k net new jobs.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeds 5.5% for three consecutive months, it signals a deteriorating labor market that reduces consumer confidence and corporate investment, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 45% of months where UNRATE has exceeded 5.5% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and decline in core inflation (CPIAUCSL) indicates a tightening monetary policy that reduces liquidity without controlling inflation, causing equity market sell-offs and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of rising FEDFUNDS and falling CPIAUCSL fails to predict negative returns in more than 50% of instances over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During a housing market recovery phase (HOUST growth exceeding 2% annually), increased residential construction activity fuels consumer spending and economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of months where HOUST growth exceeds 2% annually.

mechanism_narrative: A quarterly increase in real GDP (GDPC1) relative to the previous quarter indicates robust economic expansion that supports corporate earnings growth, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of quarters with positive GDPC1 growth.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) exceeds 3.0% for two consecutive months, it signals a restrictive monetary policy that increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 45% of months where FEDFUNDS has exceeded 3.0% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) indicates broad-based economic expansion that boosts corporate profits and investor confidence, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of rising INDPRO and HOUST fails to predict positive returns in more than 50% of instances over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During a manufacturing expansion regime (INDPRO growth exceeding 1.5% annually), increased industrial output supports higher corporate earnings and positive equity returns, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of months where INDPRO growth exceeds 1.5% annually.
